REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - OCTOBER 10, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
OCTOBER 10, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Cerritos “Mighty Mites” Youth Flag
  Football Team.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  The following Proclamations were presented:

  Tseng-Siu Wang (100th Birthday Celebration).

  Su Casa-Ending Domestic Violence (Domestic Violence Awareness Month).

  Jane Dean and Dr. Mark Chung (National Preparedness Month).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Lt. Colonel Christopher Haar, 1st Combat Engineers Battalion, displayed a
  PowerPoint Presentation describing the Battalion's mission and thanked the City
  for their support.

  Roger Kline spoke in opposition to lifetime medical benefits for future
  Councilmembers.

  Marty Grossman quoted from a social media forum and suggested alternatives
  for a Town Hall meeting for community input on budgetary cuts and a potential
  sales tax measure.

  Ayda Safaei, Metro Community Relations, distributed information regarding
  Measure M.

  Gail Grossman inquired regarding employee and Councilmember benefits, pay
  increases for certain operational employees, and suggested an updated audio
  system for the Chamber.
 City of Cerritos  October 10, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 10

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Jay Gray inquired whether documents can be posted to the website that are
  searchable in .pdf and requested the City to post the line item budget. He made
  various points regarding allocations in the Fiscal Year 2016-2017 budget.

  Anantha Narayanan inquired whether the budget document can be provided in
  searchable .pdf format, suggested a citizen budget subcommittee, putting
  employee benefits in suspension until the budget is balanced.

  Dora Clark and Ritu Gupta expressed concerns regarding traffic on Marquardt
  and sound levels exceeding acceptable levels pursuant to City zoning standards.
  They submitted a neighborhood petition for the record.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  September 22, 2016, as amended to correct Item 8A, page 6 of 9.
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of September 22, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  2016 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 10, 2016 in the amount of
  $9,939,581.75 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending August 31, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of Bid No. 1266-17, Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts Lettershop
  and Mailing Services (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1. Reject the low bid submitted by Tribune Direct due to past performance with
  insufficient quality; and
  2. Award Bid No. 1266-17 for Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts Lettershop
  and Mailing Services to Orange County Direct Mail in the amount of $13,400.00
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7F.  Award of Bid No. 1275-17 Printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts
  2016-2017 Calendar of Events (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to award Bid No. 1275-
  17, Printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts 2016-2017 Calendar of
  Events, to Advantage Mailing, Inc., in the amount of $34,927.80. In the event
  issues of non-performance arise, the project would be removed from Advantage
  Mailing, Inc. and taken to the next lowest bidder to ensure the City’s printing
  deadline, quality standards and specifications are met. This process would be
  repeated as necessary in order of the lowest bid to the highest (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7G.  Reject RFP No. 1259-17, Safety Program Training and Support Services
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, that given the non-
  responsive nature of all of the bids that were received in response to the Request for
  Proposals (RFP’s):

  1. Reject all RFP’s received for RFP No. 1259-17, Safety Program Training and
  Support Services; and
  2. Authorize staff to make adjustments to the project and re-advertise
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Gayle Kendall spoke in support of the proposed resolution.

  Sharad Gandhi spoke in support of the proposed resolution.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to waive reading of

  MUNICIPAL CODE REGULATING THE CULTIVATION AND USE OF MARIJUANA
  WITHIN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE
  AMENDMENT 2016-7* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Paul Bellenbaum inquired as to the legality for searching people's homes in
  accordance with the passage of Proposition 64.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Approve Development Code Amendment 2016-7, making the findings set
  forth in Cerritos Planning Commission Resolution No. 2016-23; and
  2. Waive full reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1008, AN ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING VARIOUS PROVISIONS OF THE
  CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE REGULATING THE CULTIVATION AND
  USE OF MARIJUANA WITHIN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN
  REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2016-7
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8C.  Review and consideration of an amendment to lease for extension of lease terms

  California, 90703 (APN 7034-017-910) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Wade Kackstetter, attorney for KIA of Cerritos, spoke in support of the lease
  amendment.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to authorize the City

  consent to the execution of the ground lease amendment and subsequent lease
  agreement, between the City of Cerritos and Lou Sobh Cerritos Saturn,
  Incorporated, DBA Kia of Cerritos for real property located at 18201 Studebaker
  Road, Cerritos, California, 90703, in such form as the City Manager shall deem
  appropriate.

  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 City of Cerritos  October 10, 2016
